Class Handlers

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.runner.Handlers
public final class Handlers extends Object
The jar: URL machinery of a runner jar: it owns the registration of Handler, the state that handler serves, and the construction of every URL the class loader hands out.

Why a jar: URL at all

Almost nothing in a Micronaut application asks the class loader for bytes directly. Micronaut's own resource loader, Flyway, Liquibase, ServiceLoader and Logback all discover things through URL and JarFile, and many of them parse the URL string, pass it around, or reopen it later. So the archive has to be reachable through ordinary URLs, and those URLs have to keep the shape those libraries already understand:

jar:file:/abs/app.jar!/MICRONAUT-INF/classes/<name>             the application layer, jar 0
jar:file:/abs/app.jar!/MICRONAUT-INF/lib/<dep>.jar!/<name>       an entry of a nested jar
jar:file:/abs/app.jar!/META-INF/micronaut/<service>/<name>       the merged service directory

The last shape is the exception to "jar 0 lives under "MICRONAUT-INF/classes/"": the packager merges the Micronaut service metadata of every jar into the root of the outer archive, and those records are addressed where they really are. See urlFor(int, String).

The nested form is the classic double separator Spring Boot's loader produced for a decade, which micronaut-core's IOUtils already tolerates; inventing a protocol of our own would break service scanning outright. Entry names are percent-encoded per UTF-8 byte, so a name containing a space, '%', '#', '?', '[' or ']' cannot corrupt the URL, and the same URL survives a round trip through URL.toString() and URI.

How the handler gets installed

jar is the one protocol whose handler cannot be contributed with a URLStreamHandlerProvider: URL.getURLStreamHandler skips the provider lookup for it, and a URLStreamHandlerFactory can only be installed once per JVM, so claiming it would take a capability the application may want. That leaves the "java.protocol.handler.pkgs" property, which makes the JDK load <package>.jar.Handler by name; register(File, Index, ArchiveSource) appends "io.micronaut.runner.protocol" to it and then flushes the JDK's handler cache by installing a null factory, because by the time the launcher runs the JDK has usually resolved and cached its own jar handler already.

None of that is load bearing. urlFor(int, String) and codeSourceUrlFor(int) build their URLs from the encoders' output with an explicit handler instance, so the URLs the class loader returns work whether or not the property took effect. The property only matters for a URL that is re-parsed from its string form by somebody else, which is why register(File, Index, ArchiveSource) verifies it and prints one warning when it did not take, rather than failing the launch.

Each of those URLs is built with a single parse, the handler's own, and no URI in front of it: that parse is where getResources spends its time, once per contributing jar. Nothing is lost by skipping the URI, because every spec is a valid URI by construction: after jar:, the encoders emit only unreserved ASCII, '/', ':' (in the archive path only) and a %XX escape per UTF-8 byte of anything else, and the jar and entry parts are joined by "!/". HandlerTest checks that guarantee once, together with the fields of every URL shape against its re-parsed string form, instead of every call paying for it.

Since:
1.0

  • Method Details

    • register

      public static void register(File archive, Index index, ArchiveSource source)
      Installs the jar: protocol handler for one archive and records everything the handler needs to serve it.

      This never throws. Every step that can fail (the property, the handler cache, the verification) only affects URLs that somebody re-parses from a string; the URLs this class hands out carry the handler instance with them and keep working regardless. Registration happens once per JVM: a second call for the same archive does nothing, and a call for a different archive is reported on stderr and ignored, because one process can only have one jar: handler and the archive is part of its identity.

      Parameters:
      archive - the outer archive, as the launcher located it
      index - the index of that archive
      source - the open reader of that archive

    • urlFor

      public static URL urlFor(int jarId, String logicalName)
      A URL for one logical entry of one jar of the registered archive.

      The URL carries the handler instance, so it opens even when the handler could not be installed process-wide. The name is percent-encoded per UTF-8 byte.

      One family of jar 0 names is not under "MICRONAUT-INF/classes/": the merged Micronaut service directory. The packager writes those entries at the root of the outer archive and records them as jar 0 records whose logical name is that literal root name, so their URL has to name the root too. That is not cosmetic. Whoever receives the URL is entitled to treat the part after "!/" as a name the archive really carries - by asking this connection for JarURLConnection.getEntryName(), by looking it up in a JarFile, or by resolving it as a path inside a zip file system, which is what micronaut-core does when it cannot list the outer archive directly - and "MICRONAUT-INF/classes/" + the name is not in the outer central directory.

      Parameters:
      jarId - the jar, 0 being the application layer
      logicalName - the entry name relative to that jar
      Returns:
      the URL, or null if no archive is registered, the jar does not exist, or the name cannot be expressed as a URL

    • outerUrlFor

      public static URL outerUrlFor(String outerEntryName)
      A URL for an entry of the outer archive itself, addressed by its real name rather than through a jar of the index.

      This is the shape the merged META-INF/micronaut/ service directory needs, because those entries live at the root of the outer archive rather than under the application layer's prefix, and it is also how a caller reaches the launcher's own classes, the manifest or a nested jar as stored bytes.

      Parameters:
      outerEntryName - the entry name as the outer archive stores it
      Returns:
      jar:file:/abs/app.jar!/<name>, or null when no archive is registered or the name cannot be expressed as a URL

    • codeSourceUrlFor

      public static URL codeSourceUrlFor(int jarId)
      The URL that identifies a whole jar of the registered archive: the CodeSource location of every class defined from it, and the seal base of every package it seals.

      It ends with a slash, the way URLClassLoader writes a directory code source, so that a sealed package's base URL is a prefix of every entry URL of that jar.

      Parameters:
      jarId - the jar, 0 being the application layer
      Returns:
      jar:file:/abs/app.jar!/MICRONAUT-INF/classes/ for jar 0, jar:file:/abs/app.jar!/MICRONAUT-INF/lib/<dep>.jar!/ for a nested jar, or null when no archive is registered or the jar does not exist

    • jarFileUrlFor

      public static URL jarFileUrlFor(int jarId)
      The URL of the jar itself, as JarURLConnection.getJarFileURL() reports it: the file URL of the outer archive for the application layer, and the jar: URL of the nested jar otherwise. Unlike codeSourceUrlFor(int) it does not end with a separator, because it names a jar rather than the root inside it.
      Parameters:
      jarId - the jar, 0 being the application layer
      Returns:
      the URL, or null when no archive is registered or the jar does not exist

    • owns

      public static boolean owns(String jarFileSpec)
      Whether the jar part of a jar: URL names the registered archive, which is how the handler decides between serving a URL itself and handing it to the JDK.

      The common case is a string comparison against the form this class produces. A URL written by somebody else may spell the same file differently, so the fallback decodes the path and compares it as a file, first by absolute and then by canonical path. Nothing here resolves a host name: a jar:http: URL simply is not ours.

      Parameters:
      jarFileSpec - the part of a jar: URL before the first "!/", for example file:/abs/app.jar
      Returns:
      true when that names the registered archive

    • openDelegate

      public static URLConnection openDelegate(URL url) throws IOException
      Opens a jar: URL that is not ours with the JDK's own handler.

      Installing a handler for jar: makes this process-wide, so every jar:file: URL of another file and every jar:http: URL in the JVM lands on our handler and has to keep working exactly as before. The URL is rebuilt against a context captured before the installation, which carries the JDK's handler with it; that is the only way to reach a handler the JDK never exposes.

      Parameters:
      url - the URL to open
      Returns:
      the connection the JDK would have returned
      Throws:
      IOException - if the JDK's handler was never captured or the URL cannot be opened

    • unregister

      public static void unregister()
      Forgets the registered archive and closes the jar files opened for it.

      The launcher never calls this: an application owns its archive until the JVM exits. Tests and tools that work through more than one archive in one process do, because registration is otherwise once per JVM. It does not uninstall the protocol handler, which cannot be uninstalled; the handler simply delegates everything to the JDK while nothing is registered.

    • decode

      public static String decode(String value)
      Percent-decodes a URL component, one UTF-8 byte per escape.

      This is sun.net.www.ParseUtil.decode without the dependency: a string with no '%' is returned unchanged, a run of escapes is decoded as UTF-8, and a truncated or non-hexadecimal escape is rejected the way the JDK rejects it.

      Parameters:
      value - the encoded value
      Returns:
      the decoded value
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if an escape is malformed
